transcript.text: Can you describe your role and key responsibilities as an Engagement Manager at your consulting firm?

I have nine years in consulting, the last five as an engagement manager at a global firm. I lead teams of four to six consultants on 9 to 12-week engagements, and I have delivered 11 of them. The one I'm proudest of was a cost-reduction programme for a manufacturing client, where we identified savings of about 14% of addressable spend. I'm applying now because I advise on decisions that someone else carries out, and I want to be the person who carries them out.
How did you manage and lead teams during the 11 consulting engagements you delivered?
transcript.anchor_quote: I lead teams of four to six consultants on 9 to 12-week engagements, and I have delivered 11 of them

transcript.text: I can't name the client or share the rupee value of the savings. Our engagement letters prohibit that. The 14% figure is already the most I can say about it.
Could you describe the main challenges you faced while leading these teams and how you overcame them?
transcript.anchor_quote: The 14% figure is already the most I can say about it

transcript.text: My leadership style is collaborative and empowering. I focus on creating a high-performance culture and aligning the team towards a common vision, while ensuring client delight.
You mentioned your leadership style is collaborative and empowering; can you share a specific instance where this approach helped resolve a team conflict or improve project outcomes?
On the cost programme I was a team member, not the lead. A partner designed the whole approach and I only built the spreadsheets.

Earlier, you said you led the cost-reduction programme with 14% savings, but now you mention you were a team member building spreadsheets. Could you clarify your specific role and responsibilities on that project?
transcript.conflict: You said you led the cost-reduction programme, but now say you were a team member and not the lead.
transcript.anchor_quote: On the cost programme I was a team member, not the lead

transcript.text: I'm not sure it is fair to say a consultant has no accountability for results. We are measured on whether the client implements our recommendations. I would rather you ask how I follow through.

feedback.summary: The candidate has solid consulting experience with leadership over multiple engagement teams and a strong collaborative leadership style. However, there is ambiguity around their specific role and ownership in the cost-reduction project, limiting clarity on personal responsibility and impact. Further clarity and substantiation of outcomes and personal accountability are needed. Exploration of examples demonstrating judgment in trade-offs, learning from setbacks, and specific contributions to peers were limited or unclear.

strengths.quote: I lead teams of four to six consultants on 9 to 12-week engagements, and I have delivered 11 of them
strengths.observation: Clearly demonstrates leadership experience across multiple consulting engagements with defined team sizes and project durations.

strengths.quote: My leadership style is collaborative and empowering. I focus on creating a high-performance culture and aligning the team towards a common vision, while ensuring client delight
strengths.observation: Provides a thoughtful description of leadership style focused on collaboration and motivating teams toward shared goals.

improvements.quote: On the cost programme I was a team member, not the lead. A partner designed the whole approach and I only built the spreadsheets
improvements.observation: There is inconsistency about the candidate's role on the key cost-reduction project, reducing credibility about ownership and impact.
improvements.suggestion: Practice a clear, concise account of a project where you had defined leadership or ownership, specifying your role, contributions, and outcomes, including decisions and results.

improvements.quote: I'm not sure it is fair to say a consultant has no accountability for results. We are measured on whether the client implements our recommendations. I would rather you ask how I follow through
improvements.observation: The candidate deflects clarifying ownership and moves to general accountability without exemplifying specific follow-through actions.
improvements.suggestion: Prepare a concrete example detailing how you ensured recommendations were implemented and what steps you took to follow up on project outcomes.

feedback.next_exercise: Choose one engagement you led fully from start to finish. Describe in 60 seconds your specific decisions, trade-offs you made, your leadership actions, and the measurable outcomes achieved, highlighting your accountability.
